full_judgment:
11. The learned Additional Sessions judge, Kishoreganj upon hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record found the accused-appellants guilty under sections 302/149 and sentenced them as aforesaid. 

 17. Mr. AFM Shahid, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the State, supporting the order of conviction and sentence, submits that the learned Additional Sessions Judge has committed no illegality and no error of law has crept in his decision which he arrived at on due consideration of evidence on record and that the prosecution has proved the motive, the occurrence which is pre-planned, premeditated and concerted action and as such they have been rightly convicted under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code. 

 18. Such conflicting submissions by the rival parties calls for consideration and of reviewing the entire evidence on record in it's some totality. 

 23. Mr. Huq seriously challenges that the story of dragging the dead bodies from the bichra of the informant to that house of Matbar Ali is a concocted story manufactured for the purpose of shifting the place of occurrence from Matbar's house to that of the bichra of informant party. But the ocular evidence adduced by the prosecution together with other circumstances have clearly proved that the dead bodies of Azimuddin, Ahad and Tenu were taken away by the accused by dragging. PW 1 has stated that the accused party took away the deadbodies of Ahad, Chand Mia and Azimuddin from the bichra by dragging through the District Board road via Telekhai bazar, were kept in the house of Matbar Ali The dead bodies of Abu who was killed by cross firing was also taken away by the accused party on their shoulders. This statement of PW1 finds ample corroboration from the statements of PW2 Wahab, PW 3 Alauddin, PW 4 Somraj, PW5, Molfu Mia, PW 6 Khurshid Mia, PW 7 A Hashim, PW 8 Alimuddin, PW 9 Md. A Halim, PW10 Malek, PW 11 Somed, and PW 12 Abdul Huq Bhuiyan. In addition to these statements duly corroborated, the Investigating Officer has also supported the fact of dragging of the dead bodies by the accused party who following the trail of bloods and marks of dragging of the, dead bodies went to the house of Matbar Ali. In the post-mortem examination reports of Abdul Ahad, Azimuddin, and Chan Mia, the doctor who examined the dead bodies found abrasion marks on the dead bodies of these three persons. Doctor Jahirul Islam who held post-mortem examination of the dead bodies has stated in his deposition before the court that injuries of abrasion on the dead bodies of Azimuddin, Chan Mia and Abdul Ahad might be due to dragging. This statement of the doctor set at rest the controversy over the question of dragging. Where ocular evidence is being supported by medical report and seizure list statement, it cannot but be accepted and we are satisfied that prosecution has been able to prove that the dead bodies of these three deceased have been taken away by the accused party by force from the bichra of PW 1 to the house of accused Matbar Ali. 

 25. Mr. AFM Shahid, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, submits that in the face of these form evidence of the prosecution witnesses, the prosecution case has been proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused appellants have committed the offence of murder and as such they have been rightly convicted under sections 302/149 Penal 

 26. Section 149 of the Penal Code by itself does not create any offence at all. It carries the liability of each member of an unlawful assembly for the act done in prosecution of their common object. The specific object of this section is to render the guilt of offence committed by one or more or several persons imputable to acts committed in prosecution of common object of the unlawful assembly. The necessary ingredients, therefore, appear to be that the object should be common to the person who compose the assembly, that is to say, all of them should be aware of it and concurring it the test of an unlawful assembly is whether act of an unlawful assembly could reasonably be inferred from some direct evidence as well as the circumstantial evidence including the conduct of the parties who constitute such unlawful assembly. There must be some element present for immediately carrying into effect the common object. A meeting for deliberation only and to arrange plans for future action to be taken individually and not jointly does not constitute an unlawful assembly. Where the object of the unlawful assembly was found to be only the giving of beating to certain persons and the highest offence which members of such assembly knew to be likely to be committed was grievous hurt in the absence of evidence of any special intention or knowledge, members of such assembly could not be convicted for murder under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code. Mere presence in a crowd cannot render any body liable, unless there was common object and lie, was actuated by the common object as set out in section 149 of the Penal Code. In essence therefore, it comes to this that members of an unlawful assembly who have an object common to all, each and every member of such assembly is actuated or animated to achieve that object and in furtherance of that common object, the same is achieved, then only section 149 Penal Code may be applied irrespective of the fact whether such act is done by one or more members of such an unlawful assembly and every member of such an assembly shall 'be saddled' with the constructive liability under section 149 Penal Code. 

 27. In the present case the object of the alleged unlawful assembly which the prosecution has sought to prove centres round a dispute over the purchase of a house and a bichra land which PW. 1 purchased from one Abdul Khaleque and the rival party Matbar Ali failed to purchase. The second motive as set out by the prosecution is over the second marriage of Ahad, brother of PW 1 who married the sister of accused Tenu. As we have seen that this is a very remote cause of motive to be attributed as a cause for such a serious violence which resulted in the loss of 5 lives and injured many. Therefore, the ancient dispute over the purchase of house and bichra land and that the second marriage of Ahad cannot be attributed to be the central common object to be shared by all the accused for taking such grave and dangerous action as to use cannon for killing of mice. It is in evidence and also it is the positive case of the prosecution that PW 11 Somed when came out from his house to-the District Board Road with a view to going to field, he was assaulted by Abdul Hamid, Alfaz and Siraj. They chased Somed upto the Bichra here on is raising alarm all the inmates about 12 in number came out and were encircled by the accused party. The accused party with arms deadly in nature arrived at the scene of occurrence and, the occurrence took place. It is stated by PW1  informant and others that they did not resist the assailants and were silent spectators. The assailants gunned down the victims one after another without any provocation. They had as many as 8-9 guns in their possession and they fired the missiles of shots and created havoc. Human acts are regulated by certain normal norms of conduct and behaviour 40/50 persons being armed with 8-9 guns and some other weapons of attack can hardly be expected to launch a deadly attack on some 8-12 unarmed persons without any provocation. This appears to be inconsistent with common course of conduct and the evidence and circumstance raises a serious doubt as to the bonafide of their truthfulness and as such does not appeal to reason. Moreover, all the PWs are partisan and interested and as they say have enmity with the accused party. Their testimony as a rule of caution should require corroboration before basing conviction. 

 35. In criminal case, it is the duty of the court to review the entire evidence that has been produced by the prosecution and defence. If after an examination of the whole evidence, the court is of the opinion that there is a reasonable possibility that the defence put forward by the accused might be true, it is clear that such view reacts upon the whole prosecution case. 

 If the guilt or innocence of persons tried for criminal offences were made a mere matter of canvassing of such probabilities, the work of criminal courts would no doubt be greatly simplified. The judicial duty is however to act in accordance with law, that is to say on evidence duly admitted and tested according to recognised principle." 

 "Both in principle and on authority, it is consistent with the safe administration of justice that the Court should draw its own inference properly flow from the evidence and circumstances and should not be deterred from the incompleteness of the tale given by each party. This principle was affirmed recently by the Supreme Court in Syed Ali Vs. Nibaran Mullah, reported in PLD 1962 (SC) 502. 

 49. In such a case as the present one, we must not be deterred by incompleteness of the tale told by the parties from drawing inference that may properly flow from the evidence and circumstances of the case. It is given out by the prosecution that motive being a dispute over the purchase of the bichra and a house from one. Khaleque by PW1 Mannan including his brother Ahad and further bad blood was created as a result of 2nd marriage by Ahad during the subsistence of his marriage with accused Tenu's sister. 

 51. The plea of alibi taken by accused Giasuddin that he was under treatment in a clinic has not been established by evidence and of selling his gun is disbelieved by the court below very rightly. The plea of Almas of selling his gun before the occurrence is not also founded on evidence. The plea of alibi taken by accused Awal is also disbelieved by the Lower Court. The plea of alibi taken by accused. Tenu is also not founded on cogent evidence and hence is rejected. Plea of alibi loses its value in the face of direct evidence adduced by the prosecution. 

 52. The plea of acting in self defence has not been pleaded or raised by the defence. Moreover, the accused are the aggressors and initiated the occurrence. In such circumstances, the case has to be decided on the basis of individual liability with reference to evidence on record. 

 55. PW 1, stated in his deposition that hearing the loud alarm of his brother Somed who along with other witnesses went to their bichra and found that the bichra was encircled by the accused party. On the order of Matbar Ali, Giasuddin.and Almas shot at Chan Mia who died instantaneously. Accused Awal shot down Azimuddin by his gun. Razzak taking the gun of Parik and Tenu with his own, gun shot down Suruj. All of them died as a result of such gun shots. Ahad in self defence brought his gun and fired few blank shots but was gunned down by Abdur Rahman. Malek shot at Surnraj and pellet penetrated into his left eye. Majid tookthe gun of Alam Gazi and shot at Alauddin causing bleeding injuries. This statement of PW 1 finds corroboration from the evidence of other eye-witnesses. PW 2 Wahab also stated that on the order of Matbar Ali Giasuddin and Almas shot Chan Mia resulting in his death. Awal gunned down Azimuddin by his own gun. Tenu Mia, Razzak shot at Suruj Ali causing his death. Rahman fired at Mad with his own gun who died. Malek shot at Sumraj and injured his left eye seriously. Majid caused gun shot injuries on the legs of Alauddin. PW3 Alauddin who was injured by the gun shot of Majid stated in his deposition that on the order of Matbar Ali Giasuddin and Almas shot and killed Chan Mia by their guns. Accused A wal shot down Azimuddin, and caused his death, Razzak and Tenu killed Suruj by gun shots, Ahad died as a result of gun shot fired by Rahman by-his own gun. Malek shot at Sumraj hitting his, left, eye. Accused Majid shot at PW Alauddin which hit his feet and different parts of his body. PW.4 Sumraj who is also an injured witness states that on the order of Matbar Ali, Giasuddin and Almas killed Chan Mia by their gun shots. Awal killed Azimuddin by gun shots. Tenu and Razzak killed Suruj by their gun shots. Ahad was gunned down by Rahman, who died instantaneously, Malek fired at PW Suruj on his left eye, he fell down and lost his senses and thereafter he was treated at Mymensingh hospital but lost his left eye. PW 6 Khurshed Mia also consistently corroborated the statements of aforesaid witnesses verbally. PW 7 Abdul Hashim, an eye-witness to the occurrence has corroborated the occurrence and stated that Giasuddin and Almas killed Chan Mia by guri shots. Awal killed Azimuddin by gun shot. Razzak and Tenu killed Suruj by gun shots and Rahman gunned down and killed Ahad by his gun. Malek fired at in the eyes of Sumraj by his gun. Majid shot at Alauddin which hit his feet. PW 8 Alimuddin also corroborated the occurrence verbally like other PWs. P.W. 9 Halim Also stated the story exactly in the same language, P.W. 10 Malek also corroborated the fact that Giasuddin and Almas killed Chand Mia by gun shot. Awal killed Azimuddin by gun shot. Razzak and Tenu killed Suruj by gun shots. Rahman killed Ahad by gun shots. Malek injured Sumraj by gun fire Majid fired at Alauddin. P.W. 11 Somed, an injured eye-witness corroborated the evidence of other witnesses in the same voice. PW 12 Abdul Haque Bhuiyan says that both, the informant as well as the accused party are his relatives and that he has no enmity with the accused party. He stated in his deposition that on hearing the sound of gun fire and seeing people running helter skelter he went to the house of Informant to the place of occurrence. On the way he found blood on kalmilata and also found pool of blood at the bichra of PW 1 and found the dead body of Suruj in the Banglaghar of PW 1. He was informed by the PW 1 and others that his brother Somed was beaten by Harriid, Siraj and Alfaz at 10 AM. Somed ran towards the bichra. Chan Mia, Suruj, Azimuddin, Wahed, Alimuddin, Sumraj, Malek, Hashim, Wahab came to the bichra and thereafter on the order of Matbar Ali, Gaisuddin and Almas killed Chan Mia by gun shot. Awal killed Azimuddin by gun shot. 

 56. It is argued by Mr. Serajul Haque that all these witnesses are partisan and interested witnesses and as such their statements should not be relied upon. But whether a witness is partisan and interested or riot and whatever be his attribute in the final analysis of the evidence, the best test of his statement is its inherent worth in point of consistency  straight forwardness as tested against the physical possibilities and circumstances surrounding the events to which such testimony relate. The Investigating Officer has also stated that the witnesses stated the mimes of the assailants to him. Furthermore, PW 12 Abdul Hoque Bhuiyan who appears to us to be a disinterested and natural witness has strongly corroborated the testimonies of these witnesses and as such there is nothing to disbelieve their statements. 

 57. The nature and extent of the fury arising out of the momentary heat and passion which resulted in the occurrence causing loss of four lives by gun-shots as proved by the prosecution evidence calls for we maximum punishment as contemplated under section 304, Part 1. But the immediate cause that triggered off such serious violence being shrouded in mystery, a lesser sentence of 10 years RI with fine may meet, the ends of justice. Accordingly  find accused Giasuddin, Abdul Awal Bhuiyan, Tenu, Moazzem Hossain, Almas, Abdur Razzak, Abdur Rahman @ Rahman guilty under section 304 Part 1 of the Penal Code for committing homicide not amounting to murder. As we have already observed the facts, circumstances and the evidence of the case do no implicate that these accused appellants acted with common object to commit the murder of the deceased and that the charge under section 149 having failed, all these accused-appellants are found guilty under section 304 Part-1 of the Penal Code. The order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional Session Judge, Kishoreganj under sections 302/149 is hereby set aside. Accused-appellants Giasuddin, Almas, Awal, Razzak, Tenu and Abdur Rahman are sentenced to RI for 10 (ten) years with a fine of Tk. 5,000.00 each, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months more.
